newsitem.title: UK: Siemens UK arms keen on telecoms expansion.
newsitem.headline: Siemens UK arms keen on telecoms expansion.

text.p: Siemens Plc, the UK arm of German engineering group Siemens AG, said on Monday it was keen to look at ways of expanding its telecoms business amid a swirl of rumours that General Electric Co Plc may announce the sale of its stake in the GPT telecoms venture on Tuesday.

GPT is 60 percent owned by GEC, with the remainder held by Siemens. A Siemens spokesman told Reuters, "We are happy with the way things are going (at GPT). Telecoms is one of our core business areas and any opportunity to strengthen it we would consider seriously."

On Tuesday George Simpson, GEC managing director, is due to announce his strategic review. This has sparked a series of market rumours on how he plans to restructure the group. Among the rumours is the possible sale of the GPT stake.

Siemens told Reuters it had already taken one move to strengthen its telecoms business portfolio. In April Siemens took management control of GPT's private communications unit which provides internal company telecoms systems. "We now have 50 percent plus one controlling share in the company named Siemens GEC Communications," he said.

Siemens refused to comment on the related speculation that GEC wants to negotiate a straight asset swap, giving Siemens the 60 percent GPT stake in return for the German group's defence business, which is up for sale.
This option was given further credence by the fact that GEC is already on a bid shortlist for Siemens' defence arm.
A decision on the sale of the defence business is expected by the financial year-end in September, the German engineering group said.
